headline: A Belgian road-safety group says Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving system often showed the wrong speed limit and drove above the limit on slow streets in Brussels.
score_reason: Specific findings, but one car, one software version and selected roads.
importance_line: Drivers using the system in Europe and regulators weighing EU-wide approval are affected, but the test used a single car, so it shows specific faults rather than how often they occur.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Carscoops, on a study by the Belgian nonprofit Johanna.be, which tested one Model 3 over about 400 km in July and says the system exceeded the 30 km/h limit on 16 of 29 Brussels road segments and showed a higher limit than the posted one on roughly 90 percent of them. The Dutch regulator RDW, which approved the system in April, told Reuters it had received the report and would assess it.
